regionAdditions.name: Gunflint Trail / Border Country
regionAdditions.blurb: Inland Cook County and Gunflint systems with long snow seasons, private and public grooming networks, and some of Minnesota's strongest late-season skiing.

regionAdditions.name: Rochester / Southeast
regionAdditions.blurb: Rochester-area natural and machine-made ski loops where storm timing, grooming thresholds and rapid thaws make the decision highly event-driven.

faqAdditions.q: How deep is the Minnesota coverage?
faqAdditions.a: The board combines destination Nordic centers, Great Minnesota Ski Pass systems, major state parks, Duluth city trails, Three Rivers Park District, Bemidji club trails, Cook County systems and Rochester grooming.

faqAdditions.q: Why are Duluth and the Gunflint treated separately from the rest of the North Shore?
faqAdditions.a: Elevation, distance from Lake Superior, grooming networks and storm response differ enough that Duluth city trails, shoreline systems and inland Gunflint skiing can produce different best choices on the same day.

trails.name: Magney-Snively Ski Trails
trails.description: A hilly 13 km Duluth city system groomed for classic and skate, with higher-elevation terrain near Spirit Mountain and strong storm-to-storm variability.

trails.name: Piedmont Ski Trails
trails.description: A 5.5 km city trail in Duluth's hills, mostly double-tracked for classic with an easy classic-and-skate loop and direct municipal grooming updates.

trails.name: Chester Park Ski Trails
trails.description: A short, challenging skate-groomed Duluth loop tucked into the hillside near Chester Bowl.

trails.name: Hartley Park Ski Trails
trails.description: Wooded classic-only loops in northeast Duluth with family-friendly terrain, a nature center and ski rentals.

trails.name: Lester-Amity Ski Trails
trails.description: Duluth's most popular city Nordic system, with classic and skate grooming and roughly 4 km of lighted skiing for early and evening sessions.

trails.name: Spirit Mountain Upper Nordic Trails
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.description: About 22 km of wooded classic-and-skate terrain above Spirit Mountain, maintained with the Duluth Nordic community.

trails.name: Grand Avenue Nordic Center
trails.description: Duluth's machine-made-snow Nordic center at Spirit Mountain with daily grooming, a full-service chalet and a resilience profile unlike natural-snow city trails.

trails.name: Movil Maze
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: A challenging 14 km Bemidji-area classic and skate system with club grooming reports distributed through Skiwise.

trails.name: Three Island Lake Recreation Area
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: About 25 km of mostly flat wooded classic and skate skiing northeast of Bemidji with active club grooming reports.

trails.name: Montebello Ski Trails
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: A compact, flat, lighted Bemidji loop that adds an after-work option to the north-central Minnesota board.

trails.name: Hobson Forest Ski Trails
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: A scenic, moderately challenging classic-only Bemidji-area trail network maintained through the local ski club.

trails.name: Bemidji High School Ski Trail
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: An easy-access Bemidji training trail that broadens the board beyond destination systems and is useful for quick local condition checks.

trails.name: Buena Vista Ski Trails
trails.sourceProvider: Bemidji Area Cross Country Ski Club
trails.description: A more demanding Bemidji-area trail system whose club grooming status can differ materially from flatter nearby systems.

trails.name: Baker Park Reserve
trails.description: A west-metro Three Rivers system with more than 9 miles of ski trail and centralized daily condition reporting.

trails.name: Carver Park Reserve
trails.description: A large southwest-metro reserve with more than 11 miles of XC trail and daily status through Three Rivers.

trails.name: Cleary Lake Regional Park
trails.description: A south-metro system with roughly 6 miles of trail, including lighted mileage, suited to after-work condition decisions.

trails.name: Crow-Hassan Park Reserve
trails.description: A smaller northwest-metro natural-snow option in the Three Rivers network with centralized condition updates.

trails.name: Eagle Lake Winter Trailhead
trails.description: A compact Plymouth-area winter trailhead in the Three Rivers system with direct open/closed condition reporting.

trails.name: French Regional Park
trails.description: A west-metro trail network with more than 5 miles of skiing and nearly 3 miles lighted for evening use.

trails.name: Glen Lake Golf Center Ski Trails
trails.description: A small southwest-metro golf-course ski loop that becomes useful during short natural-snow windows.

trails.name: Lake Rebecca Park Reserve
trails.description: A large northwest-metro reserve with more than 15 miles of winter trail and direct centralized status reporting.

trails.name: Mississippi Gateway Regional Park
trails.description: A small north-metro ski option along the Mississippi, useful for hyperlocal storm and thaw differences within the Twin Cities.

trails.name: Murphy-Hanrehan Park Reserve
trails.description: A hilly south-metro natural-snow system with about 9 miles of XC trail and daily condition reporting.

trails.name: Bally Creek Ski System
trails.sourceProvider: Visit Cook County / U.S. Forest Service
trails.description: A classic-oriented forest trail system west of Grand Marais with USFS grooming updates carried through Cook County's condition network.

trails.name: George Washington Pines Winter Trail
trails.sourceProvider: Visit Cook County / U.S. Forest Service
trails.description: A short classic-groomed pine-forest loop along the Gunflint corridor with direct USFS grooming notes through Cook County.

trails.name: Central Gunflint Trail Ski System
trails.sourceProvider: Visit Cook County / Golden Eagle & Bearskin
trails.description: A large border-country network with frequent classic and skate grooming, detailed base/snowfall reporting and one of Minnesota's longest natural-snow seasons.

trails.name: Upper Gunflint Ski Trail System
trails.description: A privately maintained border-country system with classic and skate grooming and direct reports from Gunflint Lodge and neighboring operators.

trails.name: Banadad Ski Trail
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.sourceProvider: Banadad Ski Trail Association / Visit Cook County
trails.description: A classic-oriented wilderness corridor managed through a ski-trail association and public-land agreements in the Gunflint region.

trails.name: Sugarbush Ski Trails
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.sourceProvider: Visit Cook County / Sugarbush Trail Association
trails.description: A major Lutsen-Tofte classic and skate network in the Lake Superior snowbelt with condition reporting through Cook County.

trails.name: Norpine Ski Trails
trails.pass: Great Minnesota Ski Pass / local rules
trails.sourceProvider: Visit Cook County / Norpine Trail Association
trails.description: Lutsen-area groomed Nordic terrain with multiple access points and direct regional reports, useful for elevation-driven differences from the shoreline.

trails.name: Gamehaven Park Ski Trails
trails.description: Rochester's city-maintained ski system, including the machine-made-snow Rattler trail, giving southeast Minnesota a more resilient marginal-snow option.

trails.name: Quarry Hill Park Ski Trails
trails.sourceProvider: City of Rochester / Rochester Active Sports Club
trails.description: A Rochester natural-snow ski system maintained by RASC with rental access through Quarry Hill Nature Center.

trails.name: Essex Park Ski Trails
trails.sourceProvider: City of Rochester / Rochester Active Sports Club
trails.description: A natural-snow Rochester system maintained by RASC, useful for comparing local coverage against Gamehaven's snowmaking-supported loop.

trails.name: Jay Cooke State Park
trails.description: A major state-park winter destination southwest of Duluth with groomed ski terrain in the St. Louis River gorge snowbelt.

trails.name: Mille Lacs Kathio State Park
trails.description: Central Minnesota state-park skiing near Mille Lacs, useful for storm-track comparisons between Mora, Brainerd and the Twin Cities.

trails.name: Lake Carlos State Park
trails.description: A west-central Minnesota state-park system that broadens the board into Alexandria-area storm tracks.

trails.name: Flandrau State Park
trails.description: A southern Minnesota state-park ski option where usable windows are episodic and the surface model matters heavily after storms.

trails.name: Fort Snelling State Park
trails.description: A centrally located metro state-park option along the Minnesota and Mississippi rivers, highly sensitive to natural-snow availability.

trails.name: Great River Bluffs State Park
trails.description: Southeast Minnesota bluff-country skiing above the Mississippi where elevation can preserve a storm-driven ski window longer than valley locations.

trails.name: St. Croix State Park
trails.description: A broad east-central Minnesota park near the Wisconsin border, adding another useful comparison point between Twin Cities and northern snow.
